name: Sky studies
tagline: Oil-on-paper cloud studies — painted skies, visible brushwork
technique: Romantic sky painting as in Constable's 1821–22 oil sketches: quick studies of clouds on paper with visible impasto brushwork — a sky that is painted, not photographed.
fits: a quiet cover for almost any genre
avoid: decks that need a strong physical metaphor
anything that must feel handmade in a rough way

plates.accept: Painted (not photographic) clouds, visible brushwork, upper-left quiet; no horizon.
Dusk sky bands, brushwork visible; no horizon.
Bright sky, one cloud, one faint moon; no horizon.
Blank cream paper with faint brush texture only.
One painted patch with rough edges on pure white.
One painted dusk patch with a crescent moon on pure white.
One painted patch with rough edges on pure white.

generate.base: An oil-on-paper sky study of {subject}: visible impasto brushwork, painted not photographed, no horizon, no land, no people; at most one moon, no stars, no lens effects.
generate.spot: A small oil-on-paper study of {subject}: a rough square patch of painted sky blue with thick impasto brushwork and rough unpainted edges where the brush stopped, {subject} painted in its center, painted not photographed.
generate.rules: No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark, no signature anywhere in the image.
